content: 1. Laws that criminalize abortion, impose mandatory waiting periods, or require third-party consent for abortion create significant barriers to accessing sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services. These laws should be repealed to ensure equitable access to healthcare. 2. States must ensure that biased counseling requirements and mandatory waiting periods for abortion are eliminated, as these practices hinder access to safe and legal abortion services. 3. States are obligated to reform laws that criminalize abortion and instead provide safe, legal, and effective access to abortion services, particularly in cases where the life or health of the pregnant individual is at risk. 4. Safe and legal abortion must be accessible in cases where continuing a pregnancy would cause substantial pain or suffering, such as pregnancies resulting from rape or those involving non-viable fetuses. 5. Abortion and related healthcare services must be available in cases of fatal fetal anomalies, as denying such care can result in suffering that violates the right to be free from torture, cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment. 6. Sexual and reproductive health encompasses maternal healthcare, access to contraceptive information and services, safe abortion care, and the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of infertility, reproductive cancers, sexually transmitted infections, and HIV/AIDS. 7. Survivors of sexual and domestic violence must have access to physical and mental healthcare, including safe abortion services, as part of their right to comprehensive sexual and reproductive health. 8. States must ensure that accurate and evidence-based information about abortion, including its legal availability, is publicly accessible and can be provided by healthcare professionals without fear of criminal sanctions. 9. Women with unwanted pregnancies should be provided with reliable information about where and when they can legally terminate a pregnancy. 10. Decriminalizing abortion, coupled with appropriate regulation and the provision of safe and accessible abortion services, is the most effective way to protect the right to health. 11. Criminal sanctions should not be applied to medical professionals who assist women or girls undergoing abortion. 12. Forced abortion is fundamentally inconsistent with the right to health and must be prohibited in all forms. States must take measures to prevent forced or coerced abortion. 13. Children’s access to sexual and reproductive health, including safe abortion and post-abortion care, must be ensured as part of their right to health. 14. States should consider allowing children to consent to certain medical treatments, including safe abortion, without requiring parental or guardian consent. 15. Public funding should subsidize primary healthcare services, including legal abortion, to ensure affordability and accessibility, particularly for economically disadvantaged women. 16. States must provide appropriate sexual and reproductive healthcare services to address sexual violence against women and girls, including making abortion available in cases of rape or incest. 17. Post-abortion care must be provided in all circumstances, including where abortion is illegal, to ensure the health and well-being of individuals. 18. States must train healthcare providers to deliver post-abortion care and ensure that such care is accessible to all individuals, regardless of the legality of abortion. 19. Women should have access to quality healthcare for managing all aspects of their reproductive health, including safe abortion and post-abortion care, in all circumstances.
